newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy to introduce incentives for building sector.
newsitem.headline: Italy to introduce incentives for building sector.

text.p: The Italian government will introduce incentives to encourage Italy's depressed construction sector, especially restoration work, Prime Minister Romano Prodi announced on Friday.

"One of the plans which we are working on and will introduce after the summer is incentives aimed at the building sector," Prodi told a conference staged by the national association of artisans and craftsmen.

Ministers have indicated that the government was considering helping the building industry following the enormous success of an incentive scheme introduced at the start of the year to encourage people scrap their old cars and buy new ones.

Newspapers speculated that among the likely measures would be a reduction in value added tax on building work, but Prodi ruled this out. "The plan which we are working out cannot be based on a further reduction of VAT, which we have already halved," he told the convention.

"The incentives will be aimed at the medium-to-long term and will last at least until the year 2000," he added, explaining that the measures would be aimed at restructuring and repair work rather than at new projects.
The building sector was badly hit by the wave of corruption scandals which washed over Italy in the early 1990s.
Many public work projects ground to a halt or were simply cancelled as magistrates investigated claims that construction firms paid politicians huge kickbacks to win contracts.
Constructors association Ance has asked the government to cut taxes on building work and on people buying first houses in a bid to kick start the flagging industry.
